A2a-five-kingdoms

A simple upward branching tree diagram of the five kingdoms from simple (bottom) to complex (top), with plain arrows pointing upward between levels. Bottom: a single rod-shaped bacterium (Monera). Above it: an Amoeba (Protista). Above that: a mushroom (Fungi). At the top the tree branches into two: on the left a fern and a small flowering plant together (Plantae), on the right a fish and a goat together (Animalia). Each group clearly separated with white space beside it. Soft pastel colours.
A2a-bacterial-cell

A single large rod-shaped bacterial cell drawn horizontally and cut open to show its inside. From outside in: a thick pale outer capsule, a cell wall, a thin cell membrane, cytoplasm. Inside: a tangled loop of circular DNA (nucleoid) in the middle, two or three small separate plasmid rings, many tiny dots (ribosomes). One long wavy flagellum coming out of the right end, and many short straight hair-like pili around the surface. Soft blue and lilac palette.
A2a-bacteria-shapes

Four groups of bacteria in a 2 by 2 grid with generous white space between groups (no frames). Top left: round cocci shown three ways, a pair, a short chain, and a grape-like cluster. Top right: several rod-shaped bacilli. Bottom left: several corkscrew spiral spirilla. Bottom right: several comma-shaped vibrios each with one flagellum. Simple smooth cells, soft colours.
A2a-bacteria-binary-fission

Binary fission of a rod-shaped bacterium in four stages in one horizontal row, left to right, with a plain arrow between each stage: 1) one rod-shaped cell with a single loop of circular DNA; 2) the same cell slightly longer with the DNA copied into two loops; 3) a longer cell with the membrane and wall pinching inward at the middle, one DNA loop in each half; 4) two separate identical small rod-shaped daughter cells each with one DNA loop. Soft blue palette. Plenty of white space above and below the row.
A2a-nostoc

A magnified view of a Nostoc colony: a rounded pale transparent jelly-like mass containing several twisting bead-like filaments (chains) of small round blue-green cells. In the chains, a few larger, paler, thick-walled round heterocysts. Off to one side, outside the jelly, one enlarged section of a single filament showing ordinary cells, a heterocyst, and a larger oval thick-walled resting spore (akinete). Soft blue-green tones.
A2a-amoeba

A single Amoeba, large, with an irregular outline and four blunt finger-like pseudopodia. A thin clear outer layer (ectoplasm) all around the edge and a granular inner cytoplasm (endoplasm). One round nucleus, one clear round contractile vacuole, several small food vacuoles containing food particles. On one side, two pseudopodia curving around and nearly enclosing a small green food particle. Soft grey-blue and lilac palette.
A2a-amoeba-binary-fission

Binary fission in Amoeba in four stages in one horizontal row, left to right, with a plain arrow between each stage: 1) a rounded Amoeba with one nucleus; 2) the nucleus elongated and dividing into two; 3) the cell stretched with the cytoplasm pinching in at the middle, one nucleus in each half; 4) two small separate daughter amoebae each with one nucleus. Soft grey-blue palette. Plenty of white space above and below.
A2a-euglena

A single Euglena shown large and upright: a spindle-shaped green cell. At the front (top) end a flask-shaped reservoir (gullet) opening, with one long whip-like flagellum coming out of it. A red eyespot beside the reservoir. A clear contractile vacuole next to the reservoir. Many oval green chloroplasts. A round nucleus in the centre. A few small pale white paramylon granules scattered between the chloroplasts. A thin outer pellicle with faint spiral stripes. Soft greens.
A2a-paramecium

A single Paramecium shown large and upright: a slipper-shaped cell with its whole outline covered in fine short cilia. An oral groove on one side leading into a tube-like gullet. Several round food vacuoles. A large bean-shaped macronucleus with a small round micronucleus beside it. Two star-shaped contractile vacuoles with radiating canals, one near each end. A row of tiny rod-shaped trichocysts just under the outer pellicle along the edge. A small anal pore near the rear on the same side as the oral groove. Soft blue and peach palette.
A2a-paramecium-conjugation

Two Paramecium cells lying side by side, touching and joined at their oral grooves during conjugation, with a short cytoplasmic bridge between them. Each cell has a large bean-shaped macronucleus and small nuclei; two small nuclei are shown crossing the bridge in opposite directions, one from each cell. Cilia around both cells. Simple and clear. Soft blue and peach palette.
A2a-rhizopus

Rhizopus (bread mould) growing on a slice of bread, shown in a side view. Fine white hyphae forming a fuzzy mycelium over the bread surface; an arching horizontal hypha (stolon) bending between two points; at each point a cluster of short root-like rhizoids going down into the bread; from each point several upright stalks (sporangiophores) each ending in a round black sporangium. To the right, a separate enlarged view of one sporangium cut in half showing a dome-shaped columella inside and many tiny spores around it. Soft greys, creams and black.
A2a-rhizopus-conjugation

Sexual reproduction (conjugation) in Rhizopus in five stages arranged as a row of three on top and a row of two below, with plain arrows from one stage to the next: 1) two separate hyphae growing towards each other; 2) their tips swelling and touching; 3) the swollen tips cut off by cross walls as gametangia, fusing; 4) a single dark, thick-walled, warty zygospore between the two parent hyphae; 5) the zygospore germinating to produce an upright stalk with a round germ sporangium on top. Soft greys and browns.
A2a-mushroom

Left: a whole mushroom drawn cut in half lengthwise standing in soil, showing the domed cap, the thin gills radiating under the cap, a ring (annulus) around the upper stalk, the stalk, and white thread-like mycelium spreading in the soil below. Right, clearly separated: a magnified view of the surface of one gill showing a row of club-shaped basidia, each bearing four small round basidiospores on tiny stalks at its tip. Warm creams and browns.
A2a-mushroom-life-cycle

A circular life cycle diagram of a mushroom with plain curved arrows going clockwise around a circle between six stages, evenly spaced with white space between them: top: tiny spores falling from the gills of a mushroom cap; right top: a spore germinating into a thin single thread (primary mycelium); right bottom: two thin hyphae fusing together; bottom: a dense secondary mycelium in soil; left bottom: a small rounded button mushroom just above the soil; left top: a mature mushroom with an open cap and gills. Warm creams and browns.
